regions.region: page 1 title, authors, article metadata and abstract
regions.finding: Verified the full source title. The abstract summarizes the current Bu3SnH/Ph3SnH hydrostannations and the distinct 1-equiv low-temperature EPR series; these are linked to their concrete records rather than counted again.

Classified the preceding kinetic study, earlier Hale–Manaviazar mechanism and stannylvinyl-cation theory as prior/contextual work. No current-paper experiment-specific quantity beyond the abstract is introduced here.
The paper advertises ESI, but source mapping marks SI association unestablished; no EPR procedure, spectrum or NMR/MS fact was imported from SI.

unresolved: Abstract quantities are aggregate summaries; experiment-specific charges and procedures come from later text evidence and remain machine-unreviewed.
No workspace SI association is established.

regions.region: page 2 lower-left Scheme 1 and adjacent new-route prose
regions.finding: Recorded all four current-paper preparation arrows independently and one aggregate route summary. The 41–56% four-step yield is attached to the 1→5 span, not to the last step. Later individual procedures were used only as cross-page context and reveal retained time conflicts for 2→3, 3→4 and 4→5.
Recorded Baines et al. (2005) alkyne-4 acid hydration/cation trapping as cited prior literature with THF/H2O 4:1, reflux, 83 h and 7:8=1:10.7; it is not a current-paper experiment.
Recorded Velegraki and Stratakis (2013) Au-catalyzed hydration as cited prior literature (0.01 equiv catalyst, 4 equiv water, MeOH, 25 °C, 82% 10), not a current-paper run.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right Scheme 4 and surrounding hypothesis prose
regions.finding: Classified the 14–20 network as the authors' proposed cation-trapping test. Hypothetical products/intermediates were not assigned observed yields; actual aqueous non-detections are in the page-3 Scheme 5 record.

unresolved: Scheme/individual-procedure time conflicts remain unresolved: 2 vs 3.5 h for 2→3, 19 vs 21 h for 3→4, and 1.5 vs 25 h after paraformaldehyde addition for 4→5.
Complex stereochemical structures remain source-labeled with null SMILES and unverified.

regions.region: page 3 lower-left Scheme 5 reaction header and three condition rows
regions.finding: Recorded three distinct current-paper reactions: Bu3SnH/PhMe/rt/24 h gives 21 in 43%; Bu3SnH/THF-H2O 4:1/72 °C/2.5 h gives 21 in 31%; Ph3SnH/PhMe/rt gives a 23/24 1.39:1 mixture in 67%. Each retains separate charges, staged additions, workup/purification and product-targeted outcomes.

Retained unreacted starting material, exclusive alkyne-derived 21, and non-detection of 14/15 for the aqueous reaction. The Ph3SnH prose time of 3.25 h conflicts with the later 3 h 10 min procedure and both are preserved.
Classified 25–29 as a proposed O-directed radical-addition/EH1 ring-opening/H-atom-abstraction mechanism leading to 21/23, not independent preparations.

regions.region: page 3 right-column NMR structural-assignment discussion of 24
regions.finding: The NMR discussion supports the already-recorded 24 identity and Z assignment from the 23/24 reaction; spectral peaks do not create another experiment or machine structure verification.

unresolved: Ph3SnH reaction-time conflict: page 3 gives 3.25 h, later individual procedure gives 3 h 10 min.
Unreacted-starting-material recoveries and non-detection limits are not quantified.
The 67% belongs to the combined unseparated 23/24 mixture, not either component alone.

regions.region: page 4 upper text describing low-temperature EPR examination
regions.finding: Recorded the 1-equiv Ph3SnH/catalytic Et3B/O2/PhMe EPR series at 230–250 K. Radicals 27, 29 and 31c were not identified; the main species accumulating over 10 min to 1 h is consistent with 33, while assignment of broad-singlet 32 is tentative.
Classified the 23→30→31a-c→24 and reversible 24/32/33 network as a proposed mechanism, separate from the observed EPR series and preparative hydrostannation.

Linked the 250 K EPR spectrum/EasySpin overlay to the EPR series and retained g=2.0020 plus beta-H hyperfine values 1.32 and 0.57 mT (13.2 and 5.7 G). This is characterization, not an isolated-radical yield.
Classified triple hyperconjugative stabilization and 32↔33 interpretation as mechanistic discussion. Radical populations are not quantified and 32 remains tentative.

unresolved: The EPR series lacks absolute charges, Et3B loading, concentrations and individual spectrum times/temperatures on pages 1–6.
Radical 32 is tentative; 33 is spectroscopically consistent rather than isolated or quantitatively related to 24.

regions.finding: Figure 2 depicts a possible double-vicinal beta-Ph3Sn hyperconjugative stabilization model for 33/32. It enriches the Scheme 7 mechanism and is not a new reaction experiment.
Figure 3 depicts a possible alpha-Ph3Sn SOMO-to-sigma-star delocalization model. It is a proposed electronic-structure explanation, not an observed preparation or separate EPR run.

The prose interprets reversible O-coordinated 1,2-addition/elimination and contrasts it with high-temperature 1,1-addition/elimination. No new current-paper charge, yield or independently enumerated experiment is reported.

unresolved: The degree of hyperconjugation and 32/33 population are not measured; Figures 2–3 are explicitly possible models.

regions.finding: Recorded the generalized room/lower-temperature favored 1,2-addition/elimination pathway and the >80 °C minor 1,1 pathway as a mechanism. Generic 34–44 entities and qualitative major/minor outcomes are not represented as a single experimental run.

regions.region: page 6 upper two-column continuation of temperature/time discussion
regions.finding: Retained the qualitative warning that prolonged high-temperature hydrostannation can cause Z/E isomerization. No exact duration or current-paper high-temperature experiment is printed on this page.
The conclusions restate the current hydrostannation/EPR findings and proposed radical mechanism. They add no independent reaction row, charge, yield or selectivity beyond the existing records.
